failure_summary.description: Generated code skipped a required cache update, used an unsuitable cached variable, omitted saving a result, or added redundant cache operations.
Some trajectories touched unchanged domains, missed a still-pending deliverable, or inferred a value not supplied by the user.
An arrival deadline phrased as “by” was treated as a lower rather than upper time bound.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly covers cache saves, follow-up deltas, pending deliverables, and avoiding unrelated work, so restating those rules would be duplicative. The time-bound rule does not explicitly map “by” or “no later than” to an upper bound for arrival times; clarify that phrasing to address the uncovered error.

edits.target: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`, and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`, preserving the stated AM/PM value.
edits.content: - For a one-sided bound on either `departure_time` or `arrival_time`, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X,” “by X,” or “no later than X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`; “after X” or “no earlier than X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`. Preserve the stated AM/PM value.
